Since the Index counts translations of individual books, authors with many books with few translations can rank higher than authors with a few books with more translations. So, for example, while the Bible is the single most translated book in the world, it does not rank in the top ten of the index. The Index counts the Walt Disney Company, employing many writers, as a single writer. Authors with similar names are sometimes included as one entry, for example, the ranking for "Hergé" applies not only to the author of *The Adventures of Tintin* (Hergé), but also to B.R. | Rank | Author | Birth date (YYYY‑MM‑DD) | Source for ranking | Source for birth date |
|------|--------|--------------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| 1 | **Agatha Christie** | 1890‑09‑15 | UNESCO Index Translationum – “Top 10 Author” list【Index Translationum】 | Wikipedia – Agatha Christie【Agatha Christie】 |
| 2 | **Jules Verne** | 1828‑02‑08 | UNESCO Index Translationum – “Top 10 Author” list【Index Translationum】 | Wikipedia – Jules Verne【Jules Verne】 |
| 3 | **William Shakespeare** | 1564‑04‑23* | UNESCO Index Translationum – “Top 10 Author” list【Index Translationum】 | Wikipedia – William Shakespeare【William Shakespeare】 |
| 4 | **Enid Blyton** | 1897‑08‑11 | UNESCO Index Translationum – “Top 10 Author” list【Index Translationum】 | Wikipedia – Enid Blyton【Enid Blyton】 |
| 5 | **Barbara Cartland** | 1901‑07‑09 | UNESCO Index Translationum – “Top 10 Author” list【Index Translationum】 | Wikipedia – Barbara Cartland【Barbara Cartland】 |

\* Shakespeare’s exact birth date is not recorded; the traditional date used by scholars and commemorations is **23 April 1564** (the date of his baptism is 26 April 1564).  

### How the list was derived
1. The UNESCO **Index Translationum** (the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization’s database of book translations) publishes a “Top 10 Author” table that ranks authors by the total number of translations of their works. The table (as of the latest publicly available data) shows the following top five authors: Agatha Christie, Jules Verne, William Shakespeare, Enid Blyton, and Barbara Cartland.  
2. Birth‑date information for each author was taken from their respective Wikipedia articles, which cite reliable biographical references (civil records, biographies, etc.).  

### References
- **UNESCO Index Translationum – “Top 10 Author”** (Wikipedia summary of the UNESCO database). <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Index_Translationum>  
- **Agatha Christie** – Wikipedia. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agatha_Christie>  
- **Jules Verne** – Wikipedia. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jules_Verne>  
- **William Shakespeare** – Wikipedia. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare>  
- **Enid Blyton** – Wikipedia. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enid_Blyton>  
- **Barbara Cartland** – Wikipedia. <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Cartland>  

These sources together provide a current, verifiable list of the five authors whose works have been translated into the greatest number of languages worldwide, together with their full birth dates.
